expect.note: The snapshot's own footer sha must still be the deployment's. Red here is the ALARM, not a bug in the case: it means the five offline cases listed above are grading a page that is no longer served.

provenance: T-M41-3 (M41, 2026-08-26). `src/browser/fixtures/sec10k-inspector.html` is a rendered capture of a deployed third-party page and five `fast` cases grade page SHAPE against it. Nothing read the build sha back, which the milestone demonstrated the hard way: `/api/meta` answered a different sha by `curl` at capture time than the captured page's own footer showed, and every document that recorded it recorded the wrong one until a cold review of the committed file caught it. So this reads the sha out of the ARTIFACT — the footer the captured page filled from that same field — rather than out of a provenance sentence: a document describing an artifact can be wrong about it, the artifact cannot. `live`, never `fast`: one GET, no browser, no LLM, $0, and a stale snapshot is a DECLARATION problem rather than a gate regression, so it must not be able to block a commit. Re-capturing stays out of scope for the block's own reason — a capture is evidence about a build, and re-taking it is a decision. **It fired on the tree that added it.** The snapshot is of `6b37ffa99d05`; `/api/meta` answered `33a7580964e7` on 2026-08-28. That is the third build of this target inside three milestones (6b37ffa99d05 -> 0b87705fd0aa -> 33a7580964e7), and the two intervening moves were each caught by a person deciding to look. An unreachable endpoint is also red, not a pass: an unreachable target is precisely the state in which a stale snapshot goes unnoticed (CLAUDE.md rule 4). The endpoint is a bare PATH composed against the case's own `domain` tag, never a URL in `input`: `sec10k-ground-truth-endpoint-eval-only` refuses any `<host>/api/` string there, because `input` is what a run is given. This case builds no run, and the rule is still obeyed at face value rather than by exempting a kind — an exemption is a door.

triage.red_first: Watched red both ways. Against the deployed sha: captured_at 6b37ffa99d05, deployed_now 33a7580964e7 — which is the state of the world, so the case shipped RED and that is the alarm working. Against a doctored snapshot whose footer sha was replaced with the deployed one, it goes green, which is what proves the red is about the comparison and not about the plumbing.
triage.note: What this does NOT claim: that the offline cases are wrong. They pass, and what they pass against is a page that is not being served. Whether to re-capture is the human's call; the point of this case is that nobody has to notice by hand.
